post.description: Load a csv or jsonl file's TEXT, sent in the request, into a new partitioned table placed across the cluster - for a caller that cannot put a file on the node (add_dataset reads the node's filesystem). Same parsing, table creation and placement as add_dataset; at most 16 MiB of content. Audited as dataset_added; the table then appears in list_datasets / system.datasets and can be passed to run as dataset_path <database>.<table>. (#1008) Requires orchestration:add_dataset.

content.description: the file's text, verbatim. At most 16 MiB (16777216 bytes of UTF-8); larger data belongs in a file on the node (add_dataset) or a source connection (create_dataset_from_query)

database.description: target database, created if absent (default datasets); named by the same rule as table_name

format.description: how `content` is laid out: csv (a header row, then one row per line with as many fields as the header, cells type-inferred) or jsonl (one JSON object per line)

if_exists.description: what to do when table_name is taken: fail (the default) refuses with conflict; rename saves under the next free name (_2, _3, ...) and the output's renamed_from names the one asked for

intent.description: reserved: say what you are trying to do; recorded on the call's trace, stripped before schema validation

replication_factor.description: owners per partition (default 3, clamped to the node count)

table_name.description: the new table's name: a letter or underscore, then letters, digits and underscores, at most 63 characters, not a SQL keyword. A name already taken in the database is refused (conflict) unless if_exists is rename

renamed_from.description: upload_dataset with if_exists rename: the name asked for, when it was taken and `table` is the next free one
